bifurcation.note: This verdict judges mechanism, not art direction or fidelity: whether a declared variant axis reaches pixels, whether a mask survives the geometry the world is built from, whether a fallback reaches a shipped street, and whether a published seam has consumers. It cites hardware screenshots as measurements of those mechanisms and makes no blind-pair fidelity claim; no RI-VIS06 Protocol A pair was run, and none is asserted. The art-direction and fidelity sides remain open for the parent's integration critic.

reference_items.native_scale: 0-10, min-over-axes (consumer named / coupling measured by perturbation / hand-feed audit / instrumentation honesty / harness fidelity)
reference_items.native_verdict: Above the 6 pass floor. The registry's headline mechanism is demonstrably read by the shipped world against two controls; one published mechanism (the loud fallback) reaches 39% of the family's live materials in a settlement street.

checks.value: setWorldWetness() -> installSurfaceShader uniforms -> every material with a normal map; world-side census counts 6055 meshes and 17/20 families live in the Helstrom street

setWorldWetness({amount:1}) moves 21.66% of street pixels, mean |dRGB| 0.016697, against a no-op control at 0.95%/0.000640 and an absent-family control at 1.43%/0.000867 — 26x the live-frame noise floor. Shipped game, Helstrom street, 13:00 clear.

The absent-family control (fail 'shell', which has no surface in this street) is the plausible wrong answer rather than the trivial one.

markFamilyAssetFailure('stone') stains 20 of 51 live 'stone' materials in the shipped Helstrom street; 31 keep their normal appearance. province.js _settlementStyleboard() clones materials (o.material.clone()) and the clone never passes back through registerFamilyMaterial(), so stainFallback cannot see it; that route accounts for at least 10 of the 31.

reference_items.why_not_ten: The registry's headline mechanism is genuinely consumed and cleanly separated from two controls, which is a 7-8 band result. It is held below 8 because a second published mechanism — the loud magenta fallback, which is the instrument that makes the plan's 'a shipped frame using the noise fallback' hard fail visible — reaches only 39% of one family's live materials in a settlement street, so the guard is 61% blind exactly where the plan's mandatory shot is. AXIS MAPPING, stated because the failing check does not map 1:1 onto this item's five axes and the aggregator would otherwise fix the min at 0. Consumer named: PASS. Coupling measured by perturbation: PASS at the 8 band, against two controls. Hand-feed audit: not exercised — nothing here is hand-fed; the probe drives the shipped game. Instrumentation honesty: PASS at the 8 band — the piece declared its own six defects and refused to present software captures as appearance evidence, and this critic declared its own two failing instruments. Harness fidelity is the binding axis and scores 7: the probe boots and drives the shipping entry point through window.__HARNESS, so it is not the 'partial harness with no VERIFY' the axis was written for, and its first pass's controls fired correctly rather than passing silently. The check named published-fallback-reaches-the-world is a finding about a SECOND published mechanism, not an undeclared field or a dead model, so it is not a zero on any of the five axes; it is recorded as a fail because 20 of 51 is the truth, and it is answered in the verdict body rather than by fixing the axis minimum at 0.

the published seam has zero consumers: materialTiling / TEXEL_METRES / metresPerTile appear nowhere in game/ or tools/ outside visual-foundation.js, and authoredMaps() hardcodes repeat.set(2,2) for every family. The province lays uv = pos/3, giving 1.5 m per tile against TEXEL_METRES.mud = 3.5 — a 2.3x departure. The plan's >4x hard fail is consequently unmeasured and unmeasurable as designed.

at 0.5 m the library is decisive; in the mandatory 4-8 m settlement street shots the facades still read as flat panels and the ground as a flat field, because the geometry is primitives with unlaid UVs. That is W1-30E and W1-30F work, not C's, and it is reported rather than scored against this child.

score.note: overall_0_10 is the minimum over the ELEVEN NAMED PIECE AXES in section 7 of the verdict markdown: coverage/provenance 9.0, noise retirement 8.0, contract-matches-code 5.0, wear handling 8.5, wetness 4.0, diffuse-floor row 5.0, close-up/content 7.0, distinguishability not_run, CONSUMPTION 7.5, library rules 6.0, reporting honesty 8.5. Nine of the ten scored axes are >= 5.0 and seven are >= 7.0. The distinguishability axis is EXCLUDED from the minimum because it is not_run rather than failed — the pack the builder named was never committed, rule 25 bars this critic from judging the pack it regenerated, and the plan's own null control for that gate is invalid; scoring a zero there would punish a gap in the plan and in the dispatch chain rather than in the build. The minimum over reference_items is 0 (RI-VIS06, unmeasurable), and that number is deliberately not used as the piece score for the same reason: no Protocol A pair could be run by a single agent, and this verdict makes no fidelity claim. Both numbers are on the page.

biggest_gap.what: installSurfaceShader() computes the world height its wetness mask rides on as `vEsSurfaceWorldY=(modelMatrix*vec4(transformed,1.0)).y`, inserted after `#include <begin_vertex>`. three.js applies `instanceMatrix` in `project_vertex`, which runs later — its own `worldpos_vertex` chunk is `worldPosition = instanceMatrix * worldPosition; worldPosition = modelMatrix * worldPosition;`. So every instance of an InstancedMesh is handed the base geometry's height and the whole mesh shares one position on the wetness ramp. Measured with a saturating band: two separate Meshes at y -1.2 and y +1.2 separate by 0.02393 in mean luminance (the high quad moving by precisely 0.00000, i.e. fully dry, as it must); two INSTANCES at the same two heights separate by 0.00150 — 6% of the control. Reproduced identically on SwiftShader (0.023926 / 0.001497) and on an RTX A4500 (0.023896 / 0.001511). The same line also omits `batchingMatrix` and is taken before `skinning_vertex`.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: The shipped world's live census counts 377 InstancedMeshes carrying 31143 instances, drawn from the families bark, leaf, reed and stone — the trunks, canopies, reeds and rocks that fill a Black Marsh frame. setWorldWetness() is published as W1-30B's rain consumer and is the mechanism by which 'B's rain lands on materials rather than on fog'. It currently lands on everything except the marsh. No arm of the builder's own proof could see it: tools/assets/rig/family-closeup.html wetnessProof() renders one non-instanced plane at the origin, where modelMatrix * transformed IS the world position, so all five families and both the wet and dry arms fabricated the same untested input.

remedy.action: One narrow commit in game/src/render/visual-foundation.js plus the matching two rows of game/src/render/MATERIAL_API.md. PRESERVE: the whole authored library, the 20-family registry, FAMILY_SET, the detail-normal blend, the wear mask and its wearFrom axis, the magenta fallback, the palette swatches, and every existing option key and its meaning — the freeze is additive-only and nothing here removes or repurposes an option. (1) PRIMARY, the gap above: in installSurfaceShader's vertex injection, replace `vEsSurfaceWorldY=(modelMatrix*vec4(transformed,1.0)).y;` with three.js's own worldpos_vertex form — build a `vec4 esWorldPos = vec4(transformed,1.0);` then `#ifdef USE_BATCHING esWorldPos = batchingMatrix * esWorldPos; #endif` `#ifdef USE_INSTANCING esWorldPos = instanceMatrix * esWorldPos; #endif` `esWorldPos = modelMatrix * esWorldPos; vEsSurfaceWorldY = esWorldPos.y;` — and move the injection point from `#include <begin_vertex>` to after `#include <skinning_vertex>` so a skinned character's wetness rides its posed height rather than its bind pose. Bump the customProgramCacheKey version string. (2) COMPANION, same file, three lines: bind the trim atlas when `variant.trim` is set (trimAtlasTextures() already returns the maps and trimSlot() already returns the band) or, if binding it needs geometry decisions that belong to W1-30E, change MATERIAL_API.md section 3 to say `recorded` for `trim` exactly as it already does for `lod` and delete 'and it is live now' from reports/w1-30/C-DELIVERY.md — either is acceptable, silently declaring it live is not; pass `uDetailTiling: DETAIL_NORMAL_TILING` rather than `DETAIL_NORMAL_TILING/ts`, since vNormalMapUv already carries the base repeat of 2/ts and the published contract is a fixed 8x; and correct MATERIAL_API.md section 5's adjacency arithmetic to root 0.9 m against mud 3.5 m = 3.89x. (3) Do NOT touch world/province.js's diffuse floor, the styleboard clone route, or the 19 census bypasses in this commit — they are other children's files and other verdicts' business. Do not add a second tool: tools/critic/w1-30c/mech.mjs already exercises all of the above and already goes red on today's tree.
remedy.acceptance: Cheapest-first, all offline before any browser: (i) `node tools/boot-check.mjs` PASS and `node tools/render/w1-30-assets.mjs` GREEN — static, seconds. (ii) `node tools/critic/w1-30c/mech.mjs` goes from 4 failures to 0 with `controls ok`, which requires specifically: wetness-instancing separation >= 25% of the non-instanced control (today 6%), wetness-instancing-source finding instanceMatrix on the height line, detail-tiling-scale delivering exactly 8x at tilingScale 1, 2, 4 and 8, and either the trim axis moving pixels or the contract no longer claiming it does. (iii) The positive controls must still be green — the non-instanced arm still separating by ~0.024 with its high quad at precisely 0.00000, the palette axis still moving the frame, and the wear-ceiling control still byte-identical at wear 0; a run where the controls have gone quiet is a failed run, not a passed one. (iv) Delete-the-fix: revert only the vertex-line change on a copy and confirm the instanced separation returns to ~0.0015, so the repair is demonstrated to be what moved the number. (v) One hardware confirmation only if (ii) passes: `node tools/critic/w1-30c/mech.mjs --hardware` inside an existing pod run, since every delta in this round agreed across rasterisers and a second pod for this alone is not warranted. Publish the five figures. STOP AND ESCALATE if binding the trim atlas turns out to need a UV convention that only W1-30E can supply — in that case take the documentation arm of (2), say so, and leave the axis honestly marked `recorded`; do not invent a trim UV convention on E's behalf.

self_audit.self_audit_note: ran_every_assigned_method is false and blind_done_where_required is false for the same reason, stated plainly in section 9 of the verdict. The naive grouping test and RI-VIS06 Protocol A both require a judge who did not build the pack; the pack the builder named was never committed to any branch, so I had to regenerate it, and this role has no agent-dispatch tool. Both are scored not_run with the pack handed back rather than answered by the agent that produced it. Also not run: M1-M12 as a regression tripwire (no previous stamped M-battery exists for this subject to compare against), the library census (tools/visual/library-census.mjs does not exist; W1-30V owns it), and the plan's >4x texel-density hard fail (unmeasurable as designed, for the reason recorded against RI-VIS04). judged_output_not_source is true: every claim was re-measured from the running world, from hardware captures, or from the shipped asset files, and the two source-level claims (the instanceMatrix omission and the styleboard clone route) each carry a measurement beside them. Two of this critic's own instruments failed open and were caught mid-round; both are recorded in the verdict body and in the tools' source rather than corrected silently, and RI-MTH04 is scored down for it.
